mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the reaction of metals with water is correct?

options.A: All metals react vigorously with cold water.
options.B: Only alkali metals react with cold water, while some metals react with steam.
options.C: Noble metals such as gold react with water to produce hydrogen gas.
options.D: Metals do not react with water under any condition.

mcqs.answer: Only alkali metals react with cold water, while some metals react with steam.
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metals (e.g., sodium, potassium) react vigorously with cold water. Other metals such as magnesium, zinc, or iron do not react with cold water but may react with steam, producing metal oxides and hydrogen. Options A, C and D are misconceptions: not all metals react with cold water, noble metals are inert, and many metals do react under suitable conditions.

mcqs.question: If metal X reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas, which of the following metals is most likely to behave in the same way?
mcqs.explanation: Metals that are above hydrogen in the reactivity series (such as Mg, Zn, Fe, Al) readily react with dilute acids, displacing hydrogen. Sodium is too reactive and reacts explosively, while copper and gold lie below hydrogen and do not displace it from acids. Hence magnesium best matches the described behaviour.

mcqs.question: Arrange the metals in order of decreasing ability to displace hydrogen from acids: Mg, Al, Zn, Fe.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series (most to least reactive) is Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > ... Hydrogen lies below Fe. Therefore the ability to displace hydrogen follows the same order: magnesium > aluminium > zinc > iron. Options B, C, and D place the metals in incorrect relative positions.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions will NOT occur spontaneously under standard conditions?
mcqs.explanation: A reaction proceeds spontaneously when a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal ion. Zinc is above copper, so reaction A occurs. Iron is also above copper, so B occurs. Magnesium is above hydrogen, so C occurs with steam. Copper is below zinc in the series; therefore copper cannot displace zinc from ZnSO₄, making option D non‑spontaneous.

mcqs.question: Which metal reacts vigorously with cold water to produce hydrogen gas?
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metals such as sodium react vigorously with cold water, forming the corresponding hydroxide and releasing hydrogen. Iron, copper, and gold do not react with cold water.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
mcqs.explanation: Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Zinc, iron, and magnesium are above hydrogen and readily react, producing hydrogen gas.

mcqs.question: A hydrogen displacement reaction is best defined as:

options.A: A reaction in which a metal displaces another metal from its compound.
options.B: A reaction in which a metal reacts with water to form a metal hydroxide.
options.C: A reaction in which a metal reacts with an acid or water to release hydrogen gas.
options.D: A reaction in which hydrogen gas reacts with oxygen to form water.

mcqs.answer: A reaction in which a metal reacts with an acid or water to release hydrogen gas.
mcqs.explanation: Hydrogen displacement refers specifically to the ability of a metal to displace hydrogen from acids or water, producing hydrogen gas. Option A describes metal displacement, B describes a specific case of water reaction, and D describes combustion of hydrogen, none of which define hydrogen displacement.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Which metal can be used to extract copper from its ore by a displacement reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, zinc is more reactive than copper, so zinc can displace copper ions from copper compounds (e.g., Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu). Iron is less reactive than copper, magnesium is more reactive but is not commonly used for copper extraction, and copper cannot displace itself.
